text: hey we have some documents and statements around (and memories probably) about dont use subagents and workflows and all that, well its dated. im open to seeing what has changed / if the systems have gotten genuinely better and so go ahead and start by locating all said notation, then remove it, and just write a document that isnt precontext loaded that says where the notes lived if we want to repopulate them
resolution: Located and removed the dated anti-subagent notation. Governing rules pulled: CLAUDE.md's 'Task tool is forbidden' warning, the 'DO NOT USE EXPLORE IN THIS REPOSITORY' HARD RULE, and the 'NO SUBAGENTS, NO -A' HARD RULE; AGENTS.md's 'No subagents' Discipline Rule; and the 'No Explore agent' note in the auto-loaded memory (behavior.md body + frontmatter description, and the MEMORY.md index line). Kept the unrelated HARD RULES (frozen dirs, V8 default, banned shell, self-matching pgrep) and preserved the git add -A discipline that was bundled into the subagent block (it is independently covered in Git Discipline / Discipline Rules). Left dated historical snapshots that merely mention the old rule untouched (docs/handoffs/*, docs/game/_reports/*, and the cart/app/docs supervision-vocabulary product docs). Wrote docs/retired-subagent-restrictions.md — explicitly NOT precontext-loaded — recording every removed note verbatim with its original file+location plus repopulation instructions, so the bans can be restored if subagents/workflows still misbehave against this custom codebase. Memory files live outside the repo and were edited in place (not committed).
